dedupe_keys.name: openlog drillhole visualisation and editing plugin for qgis

description: OpenLog is a QGIS plugin for visualising, managing and editing drillhole data, with 3D, cross-section and log views. Its section viewer maps log data as colours along drillhole traces or as graphs beside them, supports several terrain model outlines, projects downhole structural data as apparent dips and handles geographic, local or projected coordinates. It was started by Oslandia with a team of mining industry partners, is listed in the QGIS repository with Apeiron as author, and is funded by its industry users. It is generic in location. It is free to download from the QGIS plugin repository, with code on GitLab; version 2.0.1 of 25 September 2026 is the latest release, for QGIS 3.40 and later, with frequent releases through 2026. The pages read call it open source without naming the licence. Caveats: the Oslandia page still describes it as a beta, and it needs extra dependencies listed in its documentation. For simulation it prepares and checks the drillhole and geology data behind mine planning, ground stability and tailings models. It is related to the Western Australia mineral exploration drillholes record in this catalogue, a source of data it can display.
